publications.math_review: For fixed p in (0,1), ordinary triangles T_n counted once in G(n,p), and every positive integer sequence q_n, max over all residues a of |q_n P(T_n = a mod q_n)-1| tends to zero if and only if q_n=o(n^2). This includes q=1, bounded, composite, oscillating, arbitrarily slowly subcritical, critical and supercritical sequences. Triangle standard-deviation normalization starts at n>=3; the known ordinary 2K2 supplement starts at n>=4.
publications.priority_scope: This is a credited complete consequence of earlier estimates. Scott's 2009 report of joint work with Tateno states the smaller all-integer modulus range, the necessary standard-deviation scale and a triangle Gaussian-cell local limit theorem. Gilmer and Kopparty's 2014 manuscript Lemmas 4-5 already imply the full sufficient range by direct modular Fourier-grid summation; the supporting deduction is assembled in the current audit and is not backdated as a printed 2014 corollary. Berkowitz supplies earlier quantitative triangle input. The main probability-mass proof imports Sah-Sawhney arXiv:2006.11369v1 Theorem 1.1; its known 2K2 obstruction, Theorem 1.3, is credited. Weber supplies a finite-window/tail/Gaussian mechanism precedent only: his independent-sum theorem and constants are not imported for dependent triangle counts. No novelty, firstness, new deep method, new local limit theorem, current worldwide openness or independent-discovery lineage is certified.

publications.math_review: The full ring of integers of Q(sqrt(10)) gives a complete elementary negative answer to the equality printed in Long Question 7.2 (arXiv:1512.04620v1), using its prime-element convention and without a PID assumption. Both the unit-difference and unit-or-prime-element-difference graphs have clique number two, and the least norm of a nonzero prime ideal is two. The displayed proposed equality therefore compares two with four.
publications.priority_scope: This is a credited elementary exposition, with no claim of novelty, firstness, current worldwide openness, or independent discovery lineage. Lenstra's 1977 Proposition 2.2 already supplies the ideal-residue unit-clique bound. Dummit's 2021 notes explicitly contain the same classical ideal and norm obstruction. Long and Thistlethwaite supply the prime-clique framework; Lopez's 2018 thesis defines the same first prime graph and related higher prime-ideal-power graphs. Combining old ingredients here is not backdated as an earlier printed resolution. The exact historical priority of the full graph conclusion remains unestablished after the scoped audit.

publications.math_review: The universal nonmembership conjecture in Karpenko's 2016 Oberwolfach contribution is false at n=8. There is a 17-dimensional quadratic form phi over a characteristic-zero field F with even Clifford index 256 such that, for K=F(SB(C0(phi))) and X=OG8(phi), the original distinguished class e8 belongs to gamma5 K(X_K). The note retains the original field, special class and maximal-index hypothesis. It gives a complete negative answer to the universal statement, without asserting failure for every n or exact filtration depth.
publications.priority_scope: This is an exposition and independent explicit verification of a consequence of prior work. Karpenko's original pointwise transfer and filtration theorem, together with the previously computed Spin(18) index bound, already imply the conclusion. The index is printed in author versions dated May 2021, summarized with Merkurjev in 2022 and published in 2023. Karpenko's later analytic proof, in an August 2023 author version and the 2024 original/2025 translation, supplies the bound used in the main proof. No new Spin-index theorem or class-valuation theorem is claimed. Priority for an explicit earlier combined gamma-filtration statement and for the specific numerical witnesses remains unestablished; no firstness or current worldwide openness is claimed.

publications.math_review: Both endpoint questions in the bilinear analytic annihilator of Hayman and Lingham, Problem 7.72, have negative answers under the printed negative-kernel convention. The norm-one input v(z)=z/bar(z) on the unit disc annihilates every integrable analytic test function, while its Beurling transform is 1+log|z|^2 and is essentially unbounded. Explicit polynomials v_m(z)=z^2 sum_{j=0}^{m-1}(1-|z|^2)^j lie in the same annihilator, have norm one and have transform norm H_m, the m-th harmonic number. Each fixed polynomial has bounded transform, but no common uniform constant exists.
publications.priority_scope: This is an exposition and independent explicit verification of consequences of classical formulas, with a self-contained proof. Iwaniec published the exact nonpolynomial witness, output and primitive in 1986. Gill published the general positive-angular transform formula in 2010; the polynomial formula and harmonic-number norm follow by elementary specialization. The 2019 Hayman-Lingham book attributes resolution of Problem 7.72 to Volberg. Its cited reference 52 is the 2008 Banuelos-Janakiraman finite-p paper; the current audit did not locate an explicit full-target account there or a separate Volberg proof. This limitation does not refute the book attribution. No new solution, witness, transform mechanism, first polynomial construction, first harmonic-number calculation or current worldwide openness is claimed. Priority for an earlier explicit combined statement in the exact annihilator notation remains unestablished.
